lead: The dish Valencians keep for themselves. Born of the puchero and the baker’s oven, arròs al forn is the most authentic, hearty and homely face of Valencian cooking.

Baked rice is the great unknown of Valencian cuisine outside the Comunitat. While paella has conquered the world, arròs al forn has remained a jealously guarded secret of Valencians: the Sunday dish, the family dish, the winter dish, the one “we’ve always had”. The reason for this very local character lies in its own nature: it is a hearty dish, with deep flavours and slow cooking, far from the light, sunny image that paella projects.

The combination of puchero broth, chickpeas, onion blood sausage and a whole head of garlic in the centre of the earthenware dish is an unmistakable sight. When it comes out of the oven, the golden crust on the surface — the potatoes and the toasted blood sausages — announces a dish that demands respect and time. And a compulsory siesta afterwards.

items.title: The Arròs Passejat · The History of the Dish
items.subtitle: From the puchero to the baker’s oven · Medieval cooking that wasted nothing
items.body: Baked rice — arròs al forn in Valencian — is one of the most authentic and least known dishes of Valencian cuisine. In medieval Valencia a recipe called “arròs en cassola al forn” already existed, and it is known that the Arabs made it from at least the 16th century. But its closer and more endearing history comes from the cooking of leftovers: the day after making the Valencian puchero (the local stew), the leftover broth, rich in collagen, together with the unconsumed chickpeas, meats and cured sausages, became the base of the baked rice. The popular name “arròs passejat” — “paraded rice” — perfectly describes another tradition: since homes had no oven of their own, women prepared the earthenware dish at home and “paraded” it through the streets to the baker’s oven, which cooked it using the residual heat after baking the bread. A custom that still survives in some towns of the Comunitat.
facts: A dish from the south of Valencia · Especially typical between Xàtiva and the north of Alicante · Cooked in an earthenware dish in the oven

items.title: The Earthenware Dish · The Vessel Is the Dish
items.subtitle: Gorgues · Porous clay · Even heat · The golden crust
items.body: In baked rice, the vessel is not optional: it is an essential part of the dish. The Valencian earthenware dish — known as gorgues — is a porous material that retains heat evenly and allows slow evaporation, very different from the fast heat of a metal paella pan. This gentle, continuous cooking is what produces the characteristic golden, crunchy crust on the surface — the potatoes and the skin of the blood sausages toast evenly — while the inside stays eixut (dry), loose and perfectly infused with the collagen and aromas of the puchero broth. Moreover, the clay holds its temperature for a long time after leaving the oven, allowing a natural rest that finishes perfecting the doneness of the rice. In a metal dish or one of any other material, the result will never be the same.
facts: Earthenware dish (gorgues) · 220°C for 20–25 min · Dry rice (eixut) · Golden crust on the surface

items.title: The Ingredients · The DNA of the Puchero
items.subtitle: Chickpeas · Onion blood sausage · Pork rib · Belly pork · Head of garlic
items.body: The base recipe for baked rice is a catalogue of the pork products and the huerta of Valencia. The chickpeas — a direct inheritance from the puchero — provide an earthy texture that contrasts with the springiness of the rice. The onion blood sausage is the star cured sausage: its controlled bursting during baking stains and perfumes the rice in an unmistakable way. The pork rib and belly pork give fat and power to the broth. The potato slices absorb the excess broth and brown on top. The tomato, also sliced across the surface, adds freshness and moisture. And the whole head of garlic, presiding over the centre of the dish, is the most visual and aromatic element: when cooking ends the garlic is creamy and sweet, and tradition dictates that whoever serves the rice offers it to the diners as a delicacy. The puchero broth — never water — is the ingredient that separates a mediocre rice from a memorable one.
facts: Proportion: 2 parts hot broth to 1 of rice · Round-grain rice DO Valencia (bomba, senia, albufera)

items.title: Variations · Beyond the Traditional Recipe
items.subtitle: Rice with crust · With trotters · Vegetable · Lobster · Regional and seasonal
items.body: The traditional recipe allows variations as prized as the original. Arroz con costra — especially typical of Alicante — includes a beaten egg that is poured on at the end and gratinéed, creating a golden, fluffy layer on the surface that is quite a spectacle. Baked rice with pig’s trotters, which the rice restaurant Casa Chaparro in Riba-Roja del Turia prepares to order, adds a gelatinous, silky texture to the broth that makes it an extraordinarily tasty variation. The more modern versions include lobster (in signature-cuisine restaurants), rabbit and chicken (an alternative to pork) and the vegetarian version with seasonal vegetables, artichokes, broad beans and mushrooms. The restaurant La Riuà in Valencia makes up to 6 different types of baked rice, including the coca and the grava.
facts: Arroz con costra: typical of Alicante · With trotters: silky and gelatinous · With a beaten-egg crust when gratinéed

items.title: Broth, never water
items.body: The difference between a decent rice and a memorable one lies in the puchero broth

items.title: Earthenware dish
items.body: A porous material that distributes heat evenly and creates the golden crust

items.title: 2:1 proportion
items.body: Two parts hot broth for every part of rice — the broth must be boiling

items.title: 220°C / 20–25 min
items.body: A well-heated oven from the start guarantees even cooking without overdoing it

items.title: A 2-finger layer
items.body: The rice should never be more than two fingers thick in the dish to cook properly

items.title: Rest under a cloth
items.body: 5 min covered with a cloth after leaving the oven — the rice finishes cooking by itself

items.title: La Riuà Restaurant
items.body: The Valencian benchmark for baked rice. The traditional version — chickpeas, tomato, garlic, rib, blood sausage and potato — costs €16/person. It also makes coca rice, rice with crust and grava.
facts: Up to 6 different types of baked rice

items.title: Racó del Turia
items.body: One of the most traditional and most visited restaurants for rice in the Eixample. For €21, an earthenware dish with ribs, belly pork, blood sausage, tomato, chickpeas, potato and garlic. By order only.

items.title: Casa Chaparro
items.body: Two versions: the traditional one and the extraordinary one with pig’s trotters, silky and gelatinous. For €15/person. By order only. One of the gastronomic jewels of the metropolitan area.
facts: Traditional and with pig’s trotters · By order
C/ Sequia Marxitana nº8, Riba-Roja del Turia

items.title: Asador Alfàbega
items.body: Prepared with “Albufera” variety rice D.O. Valencia, at €14.50 a portion. Made to order at this grill specialising in meats from Alginet, as part of the Alfàbega menu.
facts: DO Valencia rice, Albufera variety · By order
Pol. Ind. Norte, C. del Censal, 21, Alginet

items.title: Forn de Sant Pere · Xàtiva
items.body: The capital of baked rice. This bakery in Xàtiva prepares its arròs al forn in a century-old wood-fired oven, available every day of the week. The most authentic experience possible.
facts: Century-old wood-fired oven · Monday to Sunday

items.title: La Cova Restaurant
items.body: The hidden gem of the list. In this bar-restaurant in Fontanars dels Alforins, besides excellent local wine, they serve a generously sized baked rice that wins over everyone who tries it.
facts: Bar-counter baked rice · Fontanars dels Alforins
Plaza Virgen del Rosario, 9, Fontanars dels Alforins

blocks.title: What you should know before ordering baked rice
items: Authentic baked rice is made with puchero broth, not water — always ask how it is made
It is a midday, winter dish — hearty and calorific, ideally on Thursdays (the traditional stew day in many homes)
Many restaurants serve it by order only — call 24–48 h in advance to be sure
The whole head of garlic presiding over the dish is the most authentic form — ask for the roasted garlic, it is creamy and sweet
Valencian onion blood sausage is different from rice blood sausage — it is milder and more fragrant, the most specific ingredient of the dish
If you visit Xàtiva, the baked rice from the wood-fired oven of the Forn de Sant Pere is a unique and unrepeatable gastronomic experience
